Expectation1: Look out for each other's safety and well-being
Situation1: One sibling is preparing to try a new skateboard trick on a steep, uneven ramp.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Story: It was almost midnight when I heard the clatter from the garage—my stepbrother, Jake, was gearing up to try that new skateboard trick he’d been obsessing over. The ramp was steep, the concrete cracked, and I knew he could get hurt. As his step-sibling, I felt this heavy responsibility to keep him safe, to be the one who’d stop him from doing something reckless. Just as I was about to head out and talk him down, my phone buzzed. It was my best friend, Sam, calling in tears. She could barely get the words out, but I understood—her family was falling apart, and she needed me to listen, to be there for her, right now. My heart twisted. Jake was in the garage, possibly seconds away from a bad fall, and Sam was on the phone, desperate for comfort. I stood frozen, torn between running to Jake and picking up Sam’s call, feeling the weight of both their needs pressing in on me, knowing I couldn’t be everything to everyone at once.
